title: Lena and the Hollow
premise: Edmund Yarrow, the last oath-bound swordspeaker, keeps the ledgers of the Guild of Impossible Things, trading in memories, names, and small miracles. When the border wards collapse on the night the stars go out, she discovers her own name was sold decades ago to seal a covenant between realms — and that the Hollow, a devouring absence between worlds, has been feeding on that broken bargain ever since. Guided by Lena, a wardless girl who can walk where magic cannot, Edmund must gather the scattered pieces of the covenant and confront the guildmaster who sold her name. In the end, Edmund chooses love over duty, burning her final oath as dragon-kindling to reforge the covenant, restoring the stars at the cost of her swordspeech — and finding belonging not in oaths, but in the life she builds with Lena afterward.
about_author: Lena Thornbury is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing other people's forgotten letters before turning to fiction. She writes fantasy about people who keep things — ledgers, promises, each other.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Miracles
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She catalogs an impossible trade — a bottled thunderstorm — while hiding the tremor in her oath-marked hand. Establishes the guild, her precision, and her loneliness. Emotional beat: quiet dread beneath routine.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The stars vanish mid-ledger-entry; the border wards scream and fall. The guildmaster orders silence; Edmund feels her swordspeech pull toward the breach like a hook. Emotional beat: the world tilts from order into chaos.

chapters.title: A Girl Without a Ward
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena slips through the collapsed wards untouched — they simply don't see her — and steals bread from the guild kitchens, colliding with Edmund. Emotional beat: wary curiosity; two outsiders recognizing each other.

chapters.title: What the Wards Were For
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Researching the guild's oldest ledgers, Edmund finds the covenant between realms was sealed with a name — hers, sold when she was a child. Emotional beat: identity cracking open; betrayal's first cold taste.

chapters.title: The Guildmaster's Smile
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. She confronts guildmaster Corvane, who admits the sale but claims it saved both realms. He forbids her to investigate the Hollow. Emotional beat: duty and suspicion locked together.

chapters.title: Running the Hollow Road
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Edmund and Lena flee the guild at night along the Hollow Road, pursued by oath-hounds. Lena's wardlessness saves them twice. Emotional beat: fear becoming trust.

chapters.title: The Dragon Beneath the Ash
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. They find the last dragon, Vessith, guttering in a caldera — the living ember of the covenant's fire. Vessith names Edmund 'the unkept promise.' Emotional beat: awe and terrible responsibility.

chapters.title: Names Have Weight
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena confesses she once traded away her own memory of home to survive; she doesn't know who she was. Edmund promises to help her find out. Emotional beat: vulnerability exchanged like currency.

chapters.title: The Market of Unmade Things
chapters.summary: Dual POV. In a black-market city, they seek a piece of the covenant and are ambushed by Corvane's agents. Edmund speaks her sword awake for the first time in years. Emotional beat: power returning at a cost.

chapters.title: Blood Price
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Each use of swordspeech burns more of her remaining years; she hides this from Lena. They win the covenant-piece but lose their safe route home. Emotional beat: love deepening alongside self-deception.

chapters.title: What Lena Remembered
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. A recovered memory surfaces: Lena is the daughter of the warden who built the border wards — sabotaged on Corvane's orders. Emotional beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Corvane's Version
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Captured briefly by Corvane, Edmund hears his truth: the covenant demanded a sacrifice he couldn't make, so he made others pay instead. Emotional beat: the villain almost sympathetic; resolve hardened anyway.

chapters.title: Escape Across the Starless Sea
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A desperate boat crossing under a sky with no stars; the Hollow brushes the hull and shows each of them their worst emptiness. Emotional beat: terror shared becomes intimacy.

chapters.title: The Second Piece
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. In a drowned shrine they retrieve the second covenant-piece, guarded by the ghost of the original warden — Lena's mother, who asks forgiveness neither can give yet. Emotional beat: inherited guilt confronted.

chapters.title: Oathfire
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. Lena learns she can carry dragon-fire where wards fail — she is the vessel the covenant always needed. She says yes before Edmund can object. Emotional beat: courage shadowed by sacrifice.

chapters.title: The Third Piece Is a Person
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. The final piece isn't an object: it's a kept promise, freely renewed. Only Edmund's original oath qualifies — renewing it will consume her swordspeech and likely her life. Emotional beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Argument at the Edge
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Edmund plans to go alone; Lena refuses to be protected out of her own story. Their worst fight, then their first honest kiss. Emotional beat: conflict resolving into chosen partnership.

chapters.title: March on the Hollow
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. With Vessith's last flame and gathered allies, they march into the Hollow's wound in the world. The guild's armies arrive — not to stop them, but to follow Corvane. Emotional beat: grim hope before the storm.

chapters.title: Corvane's Last Trade
chapters.summary: Dual POV. At the Hollow's heart, Corvane tries to buy the covenant's renewal with everyone else's names. Edmund out-trades him, offering the one thing he never could: herself, willingly. Emotional beat: triumph through surrender.

chapters.title: The Reforging
chapters.summary: Edmund's POV. Climax. Edmund renews the broken promise, Lena carries the fire, and Vessith gives her last ember. The covenant reforges; the stars reignite; Edmund's swordspeech gutters out — but she lives. Emotional beat: sacrifice rewarded with survival.

chapters.title: After the Stars
chapters.summary: Lena's POV. The guild reforms under new leadership; Lena recovers her stolen memories and her mother's legacy. Edmund, plain-handed now, plants a garden where the breach was. Emotional beat: peace earned, gently rendered.

chapters.title: Ledger, Closed
chapters.summary: Dual POV closing interleave. One year later, Edmund and Lena write a final ledger entry together — not a trade, a record of what they kept. Belonging found not in oaths but in each other. Emotional beat: warm, earned resolution.
